text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The government and legislators have not considered most of the proposals forwarded by the Business Centre Club (BCC), Poland's biggest private employers' lobby, in decisions and regulations made this year, BCC said.

- Over 95 percent of workers of Rzeszow province's CPN fuel distribution chain voted in a referendum that they would be ready to strike to guarantee their social security benefits and employment conditions during restructuring of the fuel sector.

- The Bystrzyca paper and cardboard plant has contracted a corrugated board production line from France's Martin SA and a carboard cutter facility from the Swiss Bobst SA. The two contracts are worth 8.1 million zlotys.
NOWA EUROPA

- The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, will increase interest rates to counteract a lowering of the rates by banks and limit consumer credits, the NBP president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.

- Germany's biggest reinsurance firm, Munich Re, will enter the Polish market soon. The company recently acquired a significant stake in the Alte Leipziger Europa insurance company which controls the Sopot-based STU Hestia Insurance firm, Hestia's spokesman Wojciech Fulek said.
- The food sector holding controlled by the listed Animex food trader and producer will earn 30 million zlotys in 1997, Animex said.
- The listed Centrostal metal trader's net profit in the first three quarters of 1996 was 1.29 million zlotys, the company said.
- The listed Mostostal Export has increased its controlling stake in the Ziebice fruit and vegetable processing plant to 97.86 percent, Mostostal said.
- The listed Pekpol meat processor and trader has financed construction of a hotel and restaurant complex in the Zakopane mountain resort, which cost 2.3 million zlotys to build.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's consumer prices grew by 1.3 percent in November and by 17.1 percent since January, the Central Statistical Office said.
- The Gdynia shipyard has finished building the Magnavia, a container vessel contracted by Bremen-based Hermann Dauelsberg. The ship is 188 metres long and 30 metres wide.
ZYCIE

- The Gdansk refinery has received a $100 million loan from a consortium of 14 banks led by Merrill Lynch and including Bank of America, Banka Commerciale Italiana, Citibank Poland, Bank Austria, Korea Longterm Credit Bank, and Deutschland Bank AG.
- The Wroclaw municipality plans to issue municipal bonds worth 50 million zlotys and sell them in a public offer.
- In the first 11 months of 1996, 43,079 flats were completed, which showed an 18 percent decline compared with the same period last year.
- Poland's export revenues in the first 10 months of this year were $19.828 million, which showed a 5.4 percent increase compared with the same time last year.
PARKIET

- The listed Animex food producer and trader hopes to recover at least part of the 17.3 million zlotys owed by the finance ministry in connection with the government's intervention meat purchases between 1984 and 1989.

- In the first three quarters of 1996 the net asset value of the National Investment Fund (NFI) Hetman was 453.35 million zlotys, while the net loss of the fund was cut to 49.22 million zlotys, NFI Hetman said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
